title: Field Ops: Rapid Retrofit Pocket Deck (wip)
content:
Purpose: ultra-compact, field-facing slide pack + one-pager for SEs and AE/CS to triage and "retrofit" a live pilot when inference quality, latency, or cost drift threaten closure. Not a full playbook — this is a lightweight kit to buy time, preserve trust, and keep the pilot running while engineering performs a proper fix.

Audience: Sales Engineers (primary), AE/CS for customer-facing scripts, On-call SRE/Platform eng for rapid mitigation.

Topline elevator (30s): 
- When a pilot starts sliding on latency or per-token cost, this deck gives a three-move play to stabilize: (1) fast diagnosis checklist, (2) low-risk runtime fallbacks, (3) customer-facing framing + rollback options.

Slide 1 — One-line hook + decision window (30–90m):
- Hook: "Keep the customer running, avoid noisy escalations, and buy engineering 48–72h."
- Decision window: immediate (minutes), short (hours), remediation (days).
Speaker note: set expectations with AE: we can stabilize quickly, but a proper root-cause may take a dev cycle.

Slide 2 — Quick triage checklist (do these in parallel):
- What changed? (model version, prompt, traffic spike, input distribution)
- Check tokens-per-request and average sequence length last 60m vs baseline
- Verify route: is traffic hitting a fallback or different model variant?
- Check rate limits / queue build-up in runtime metrics
- Inspect top-5 slow requests (trace IDs) and sample outputs for quality drift
- Confirm billing anomalies (unexpected surge in quantized fallbacks or retries)

Slide 3 — Fast mitigation moves (ordered by risk):
1) Enable conservative prefix caching for recurring prompts (low risk)
2) Switch to compatible lower-cost/latency model variant if available (e.g., gptx-compact)
3) Apply latency budget gating: respond with partial/summary then stream remainder (customer opt-in)
4) Temporarily reduce max tokens or set stricter stop sequences (high impact on output)
5) Throttle non-critical background routes and reroute to dedicated capacity

Speaker note: communicate each change and expected visible impact to AE/CS before applying. Prioritize low-customer-impact moves first.

Slide 4 — Canned SE scripts (customer-facing)
- Script A (latency): "We see a transient increase in request latency driven by a change in input patterns. We can toggle a lower-latency model variant for the next 48 hours while we analyze the root cause; outputs will be similar, and we’ll monitor together."
- Script B (cost): "We can reduce token consumption by enabling prefix caching and tightening generation length—this typically reduces your per-request cost by 20–40% without changing the core behavior."
- Script C (quality fallback): "If we need to fall back to a smaller model, we propose doing it behind a canary flag for 10% of traffic, then expand if all looks good."

Slide 5 — Rapid canary checklist (10–30m)
- Canary size and KPIs: start with 5–10% of traffic, monitor latency, p95, token cost, and a small curated quality set (3–5 prompts)
- Auto-rollback triggers: p95 exceeds baseline +200ms for 3 consecutive windows OR quality score drop > 0.15 on curated set
- Logging: add clear tag to canary requests for audit

Slide 6 — Minimal evidence pack for AE (one-pager to share with customer)
- What we observed (metrics snapshot)
- What we did (actions applied, duration)
- What to expect (next 48–72h and owner)
- Contact path for escalations

Slide 7 — Tradeoff matrix (concise)
- Rows: Move (caching, model switch, throttling, reduce max tokens)
- Columns: Risk to quality, Time to apply, Reversibility, Expected cost delta
- Quick scoring: choose moves with low risk & high reversibility first

Slide 8 — Runbook excerpt for eng-on-call (tech details)
- Prompts to run in observability: kpi_lat_p95(last_60m), tokens_per_call(avg_5m), kv-cache-hit-rate
- Command snippets (examples):
  - Toggle model route: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/routes/switch -d '{"route":"pilot123","model":"gptx-compact-v2"}' (ops account)
  - Enable prefix cache: Admin toggle -> /admin/cache/prefix/pilot123 -> set ttl=300s
- Quick rollback: revert route command and flush prefix cache if quality drops

Slide 9 — Measured examples (benchmarked snippets for field reference)
- Example: switching from baseline-large -> compact-v2 cut p95 from 720ms -> 310ms, cost -38% in sample workload (seq len 512).
- Example: enabling prefix caching reduced tokens-per-call by ~22% on contractual document generation workload.

Slide 10 — Post-mitigation backlog & RCA plan
- Lock-in items for eng: detailed trace capture, model variant perf profile, kernel/quantization fallback analysis
- Timeline: initial mitigation (0–6h), stabilized pilot (6–72h), emulator/repro (2–7d), patch & release (1–3 sprints)

Appendix — Shortcheck templates for SEs (copy/paste into Slack/email)
- "Heads up: We recommend a temporary model route switch for <pilot-id> to reduce latency while we investigate. Expected changes: p95 delta -400ms, cost -30%. Approve? (yes/no)"
- Audit snippet: "Mitigation applied: model=compact-v2, canary=10%, started=2025-11-18T14:43Z, expected review=2025-11-19T10:00Z"

Risk log (for sales ops handoff):
- Risk: customer perceives fallback as downgrade -> Mitigation: use canary + side-by-side quality comparison and transparent framing
- Risk: billing spike during mitigation due to retries -> Mitigation: monitor billing minute-resolution, temporary caps on retries

Metrics to collect during retrofit (minimum):
- p50/p95 latency, tokens_per_call, kv-cache-hit-rate, top-10 trace ids with slowest durations, quality score on curated set (binary pass/fail + short note)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need sample small curated prompt set for top 3 pilot archetypes (sales to provide examples)
- Confirm exact admin API endpoints and required auth scopes for AE/SE access (ask infra team)
- Add a short A/B snippet that SEs can run in-customer to compare outputs in <5m
- Template for post-mitigation customer note (legal sign-off?)

Action items (next 48h):
- SE: assemble curated prompts for the active pilot and attach to ticket (owner: Marco)
- Ops: create a pre-approved compact-model route for pilot toggles (owner: Riley)
- Eng: instrument quick-trace view for pilot-specific traces (owner: Sofia)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep language non-technical when talking to execs; provide 1-line reassurance + timeline
- Avoid promising permanent fixes in customer comms; frame as short stabilization plan + follow-up RCA

Revision history:
- v0.1 (2025-11-18): initial draft of quick moves and scripts
- v0.2 (2025-12-02): added runbook snippets, measurement examples, and action items

End of doc — live working draft.
